column1: # .github/security-resolvers.tsv — every function that resolves a security
# setting, and the fail-closed table test that owns it.
# A resolver reads a setting from the environment, a file, a database row or
# a probe, and returns the value that decides whether something is enforced.
# Each one owes a table test over {absent, empty, malformed, unreadable,
# probe error}, with every case asserting the CLOSED outcome.
# This file is the other half of failopenlint's FO04 rule. FO04 refuses a
# security setting read inline, because a setting parsed inline cannot be
# table-tested; this file is what makes 'declared resolver' mean 'tested'
#   covered   `test` names the test(s) that exercise the closed outcomes. The
#             gate fails if no test by that name exists.
#   pending   no fail-closed table test yet. `cite` names the issue that will
# The gate also fails when the named symbol is no longer declared in the
# named file, so a renamed or deleted resolver cannot leave a row behind
